project_overview: This application appears to be a learning management system (LMS) with a focus on student data and course offerings. The architecture utilizes Vue.js for the front-end, suggesting a component-based approach.  The structure reveals a layered architecture with distinct components for registration, student data management, course exploration, and user authentication.  The presence of multiple 'iLike' related components suggests a specific branding or product identity within the LMS.

layers.description: Implements application rules and handles data manipulation.
Provides low-level utilities and supporting functions.

macro_trends.title: High Prop Drilling in Vue Components
macro_trends.description: Several Vue components (e.g., iLikeDashboard, iLikeLanding) receive a large number of props, suggesting potential performance issues and decreased component reusability. Prop drilling can create tight coupling and makes the components difficult to manage and test.

macro_trends.title: Potential State Management Fragility
macro_trends.description: While not explicitly evident, the various 'iLike' components potentially share state, increasing the risk of inconsistencies if not managed carefully. A more robust state management solution (e.g., Vuex) would mitigate this risk.

key_workflows.name: Student Registration Workflow
key_workflows.description: The 'registerLearner.js' module, coupled with potential front-end components, drives the student registration process. This workflow represents a critical path for new user onboarding.

key_workflows.name: Course Data Display Workflow
key_workflows.description: The  'iLikeDashboard.vue', 'iLikeLanding.vue' and 'iLikeCourses.vue' components are likely involved in presenting course information to the user, requiring efficient data fetching and rendering.
